faq.a: Yes. With the script parsed into structured shots and each shot carrying cinematography metadata, a composer can assemble a complete prompt per shot. ACT 3 AI does this automatically for both video prompts and first-frame prompts.

faq.q: Do auto-written prompts produce worse results than hand-written ones?
faq.a: For a single hero shot, a skilled human writing carefully can win. Across hundreds of shots, assembled prompts win decisively, because they carry identical character and set descriptions every time and never get tired. The practical answer is both: generate everything, hand-tune the shots that matter.

faq.q: Can I see and edit the generated prompt?
faq.a: Yes. The AI prompt editing panel exposes it for direct editing, and a "Copy Prompt" utility extracts the exact text.

faq.q: Does this work for models other than Veo?
faq.a: Yes. Routing covers Veo 3, Runway, FLUX, SDXL, ComfyUI, Hunyuan and Wan 2.1, with an adapter layer per engine and automatic selection based on style, complexity and cost.

faq.q: How does prompt automation help with continuity?
faq.a: It is the main mechanism. Because every prompt references the same character, wardrobe and set definitions, the description never drifts. Combined with per-character LoRA training, identity holds across dozens of renders. Our continuity guide covers the full set of practices.

faq.q: What if I only have a story idea, not a script?
faq.a: AI story expansion turns a paragraph or logline into a full screenplay with beats, scenes and dialogue, which then feeds the same prompt pipeline. Articles, books, Wikipedia pages and pasted text also work as source material.
